chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
A time will come over the people when nothing will remain of the Qur'an except its script, and nothing of Islam except its name,
and their mosques on that day will be busy with construction, but desolate with regard to guidance,
their inhabitants and builders are the worst of the people of the earth,
from them mischief will spring up, and towards them all wrong will turn,
they cast back those who isolate themselves from it into it, and they drive those who lag behind it towards it,
Says Allah, the Glorified: 'I swear by Myself that I shall send upon them an evil wherein the endurer would be bewildered,'
and He would do so. We seek Allah’s pardon from stumbling through neglect.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the decline of Islamic guidance according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) foretells an era of 'form without substance,' where mosques are architecturally full but spiritually barren, inhabited by the 'worst of the earth' who become the epicenter of fitnah. This narration is central to Shia eschatological discourse, illustrating the distinction between the physical presence of worship and the spiritual reality of guidance, culminating in Allah’s oath to send a trial that bewilders even the wise. The narrator’s closing supplication highlights the collective responsibility to guard against this spiritual negligence.
